title: Telling My Parents I'm Switching Majors, Again
script: Yusuf: [hesitant] Dad, before you say anything, I want to explain properly this time, not just blurt it out like I did with the last change.
Father: [wary] Alright. I'm listening, though I'll admit my stomach dropped a little when you called instead of texting.
Yusuf: [earnest] I'm switching out of engineering. Not because I'm struggling, my grades are fine, but because I've realized I chose it for reasons that don't actually hold up anymore.
Father: [measured] What reasons were those, exactly?

Yusuf: [candid] Mostly that it seemed sensible, stable, the kind of thing that wouldn't provoke an argument at dinner. I never sat down and asked whether I actually wanted to spend forty years doing it.
Father: [concerned] And economics, of all things? That feels like trading one narrow path for an even narrower one.

Yusuf: [patient] I understand the concern, genuinely, but it's less narrow than it looks from the outside. It opens into policy work, research, even data analysis, fields I've actually stayed up late reading about voluntarily.
Father: [skeptical] Voluntarily reading about something and building a stable career from it aren't quite the same undertaking, son.
Yusuf: [steady] No, they're not, and I'm not pretending this is risk-free. But staying in engineering out of inertia felt like a slower, quieter kind of risk that nobody was naming out loud.
Father: [softening] I suppose I worry less about the subject itself and more about watching you switch course a second time and wondering if a third change is coming.
Yusuf: [honest] That's a fair worry, and I can't promise certainty. What I can promise is that this decision came from actually examining what I want, not from panic or boredom.
Father: [thoughtful] That distinction matters to me more than you might realize. Your uncle switched fields three times chasing whatever seemed easiest, and it cost him years.
Yusuf: [firm] I know his story. It's partly why I've been so deliberate about this, talking to people already working in the field before committing to anything.
Father: [relenting] Alright. I still have reservations, but I'd rather you pursue something examined than something merely convenient. Walk me through the transfer requirements.
